author: Kennedy Owens
title: DeSantis urges Panhandle residents to evacuate as Hurricane Isaias approaches
text:
TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Gov. Ron DeSantis urged residents across Florida’s Panhandle to finalize hurricane preparations Thursday as Hurricane Isaias approaches the Gulf Coast, bringing threats of storm surge, flooding and tornadoes.
Speaking from the state’s new Emergency Operations Center, DeSantis said the storm is expected to make landfall late Friday night or early Saturday morning, with tropical storm-force winds arriving as early as Friday afternoon.
“We are assuming that this could reach Category 3 status,” DeSantis said, adding that officials are preparing for a major hurricane despite forecasts suggesting the storm could weaken before landfall.
🚨 MAJOR BREAKING: Gov. Ron DeSantis warned that Hurricane Isaias could reach Category 3 strength and cover most of the Florida Panhandle if it enters near Pensacola Bay, urging residents to prepare while cautioning @GovRonDeSantis: "So this is a pretty big lopsided storm on the east side, which means if it enters in Pensacola Bay, it’s pretty much going to cover most of the Florida panhandle." "We are assuming that this could reach Category 3 status."
— Florida’s Voice (@FLVoiceNews)[October 8, 2026]
DeSantis warned that the storm’s eastern side could bring significant impacts across the Panhandle, including five to seven feet of storm surge and flooding in areas already saturated by recent rainfall.
🚨 JUST IN: Gov. Ron DeSantis that Florida has staged more than 1,000 generators, a half-million gallons of gasoline, 1 million gallons of diesel, more than 3 million MREs and 1.1 million bottles of water ahead of Hurricane Isaias, with tolls waived on the Garcon Point Bridge, Spence Parkway and Mid-Bay Bridge to speed evacuations @GovRonDeSantis: "The Florida Division of Emergency Management is coordinating with all local counties to address resource requests as well as to position key equipment ahead of the storm." "More than 6,000 utility linemen and restoration personnel are standing by to support power restoration during the storm."
— Florida’s Voice (@FLVoiceNews)[October 8, 2026]
Several counties, including Bay, Escambia, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Walton, Franklin and Gulf, have issued evacuation orders for vulnerable areas.
The governor outlined statewide preparations, including:
- More than 6,000 utility workers standing by for power restoration.
- Approximately 5,000 Florida National Guard members expected to be mobilized.
- More than 1,000 generators and 1.1 million bottles of water staged or available.
- More than 3 million ready-to-eat meals prepared for distribution.
- More than 300 Florida Highway Patrol troopers ready to assist with emergency operations.
DeSantis also announced toll suspensions on the Garcon Point Bridge, Spence Parkway and Mid-Bay Bridge to support evacuation efforts.
Florida Division of Emergency Management Director Jared Perdue said officials are coordinating with all 67 counties and federal partners to position resources ahead of the storm.
🚨 WATCH: Gov. Ron DeSantis urged residents under evacuation orders in Bay, Escambia, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Walton, Franklin and Gulf counties to leave zones A and B and other low-lying areas as Hurricane Isaias threatens 5 to 7 feet of storm surge @GovRonDeSantis: “You don’t need to get in your car and drive to South Carolina… you can evacuate miles, you don’t need to do hundreds of miles.” "Let the storm pass and then go on and get everything situated again."
— Florida’s Voice (@FLVoiceNews)[October 8, 2026]
Residents were urged to stock up on food, water and fuel, prepare for power outages and follow local evacuation orders.
“You still have time to do it, but the time is running out,” DeSantis said.
Residents can find evacuation and shelter information at FloridaDisaster.org.
